title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2610.13092v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost. However, it remains unclear whether such local savings can be translated into efficient and reliable task completion. In this paper, we investigate this efficiency transfer across five agents in two representative application settings, embodied tasks in ALFWorld and mobile app use in AndroidWorld. Across 4,500 task executions, we jointly evaluate task effectiveness, decision-level and task-level resource use, and execution behavior. Experimental results show that Jev integration substantially reduces decision cost and latency across all five agents, with task-level gains varying by workflow. Task success remains close to baseline levels on ALFWorld and declines more substantially in two mobile agents

translated_title: 当更快的决策无法造就更好的智能体：Jev在智能体工作流中的实证研究
translated_abstract: AI智能体依赖反复的决策来完成任务，而大语言模型（LLM）通常充当其核心决策者。近期Jev的出现为使这些决策更快、成本更低提供了机会。然而，这种局部节省能否转化为高效且可靠的任务完成仍不清楚。本文在两个代表性应用场景——ALFWorld中的具身任务和AndroidWorld中的移动应用使用——中，对五个智能体的效率传递进行了研究。在4,500次任务执行中，我们综合评估了任务有效性、决策级与任务级的资源使用情况以及执行行为。实验结果表明，集成Jev在所有五个智能体上都显著降低了决策成本和延迟，但任务级收益因工作流而异。在ALFWorld上，任务成功率保持在接近基线的水平，而在两个移动智能体中则出现了更大幅度的下降。
tldr: 本研究通过在ALFWorld和AndroidWorld上对五个智能体进行4,500次任务执行的实证分析发现，引入Jev虽能显著降低决策成本与延迟，但这种局部效率提升并不必然转化为更好的任务表现——具身任务的成功率接近基线，而两个移动智能体的成功率却明显下降。
en_tdlr: An empirical study of 4,500 task executions across five agents in ALFWorld and AndroidWorld shows that integrating Jev substantially reduces decision cost and latency, but these local savings do not uniformly translate into better task success—performance remains near baseline on embodied tasks while declining substantially in two mobile agents.
